stem: A homeowners policy written on an HO-3 has Coverage A, B and C. Which statement about the cause of loss is correct?
options: Special (open peril) form on Coverage A, broad named peril on Coverage C
Broad named peril on all three coverages
Special (open peril) form on all three coverages
Basic named peril on Coverages A and B only
explanation: HO-3 is special/open peril on A and B, but broad named peril on C. HO-5 uses special form on all three.

stem: Which statement about the HO-2 policy is correct?
options: Broad named peril coverage applies to Coverages A, B and C
It is written on the special (open peril) form
explanation: HO-2 uses broad named perils for Coverages A, B and C.

stem: The HO-4 (renters) form differs from the HO-3 in that:
options: It provides replacement cost on personal property
Coverage B is excluded from the policy
Coverages A and B are not needed, and 10% of Coverage C applies to tenants improvements
explanation: The renter does not insure the building or other structures. The manual describes 10% of Coverage C for tenants' improvements.

stem: An HO-6 condominium unit owners policy is written with:
options: Special (open peril) coverage on Coverage A only
Broad named perils on Coverages A, B and C
Broad named perils on Coverages A and C, and no Coverage B
explanation: The manual's HO-6 comparison gives Coverages A and C and no Coverage B; the association insures shared building areas.

stem: Which of these describes a DP-3 dwelling policy?
options: Replacement cost valuation with an 80% co-insurance requirement
Replacement cost with no co-insurance requirement
Actual cash value with no co-insurance requirement
Actual cash value with an 80% co-insurance requirement
explanation: DP-3 is special form, replacement cost, with an 80% coinsurance requirement in the manual's comparison.

stem: The dwelling policy is best described as:
options: A liability policy with no property coverage
A property policy, not a package policy
A package policy providing property and liability
explanation: The DP is a property policy; personal liability can be added as an option.

stem: A mobile home may qualify for a mobile homeowners policy (MH) when it:
options: Is parked on a rented lot
Is permanently located, skirted, tied down and has its wheels removed
Is used part of the year as a vacation home
explanation: The manual lists permanently located, skirted, tied down, and wheels removed. It also says the policy does not cover the home while moved.

stem: The farmowners policy is described in the manual as:
options: A standalone policy unrelated to homeowners
A spin-off of the homeowners policy
explanation: The manual includes a farmowners policy based on the homeowners policy as one of its two types.

stem: Under the farmowners policy, custom combining is covered when the receipts for such activities are:
options: Less than $2,000 total for the policy period
explanation: The manual states the receipts for custom combining must be less than $2,000 per year.

stem: Which business is eligible for a Business Owners Policy?
explanation: Apartments are included on the manual's eligible list. Restaurants, auto repair, and amusement places are listed as ineligible.

stem: Maximums that apply to the Business Owners Policy include:
options: No maximums-the BOP is written on any size of business
6 stories, 100,000 sq ft (max 25,000 in any one business), $3,000,000 gross receipts
explanation: Those are the BOP maximums printed in the manual.

stem: The Commercial Package Policy differs from the Commercial Property policy because:
options: It is a single property form for small businesses
It is customizable and written for larger businesses, combining coverage parts
explanation: The CPP is a customizable structure for larger risks with separate coverage parts, including commercial property, inland marine, CGL, and crime.

stem: Which property may NOT be insured by an inland marine form, per KSA 40-3-22?
explanation: The manual says KSA 40-3-22 bars merchandise held in storage, among other listed property.

stem: Which is NOT one of the three categories of property limited to inland marine coverage by state law?
options: Unique and unusual instruments of communication and transportation
explanation: The manual says real property and building contents cannot be insured using inland marine forms.

stem: Coverage for a customer's vehicle left with a repair shop is best described as:
options: Personal property coverage under Coverage C of the HO
Bailee's customer coverage, available inland marine
A liability coverage under Coverage A of the CGL
explanation: The manual identifies bailee's customer coverage for property in the business's care, custody, and control.

stem: Under a special (open peril) property form, the exclusions section:
options: Names the perils that ARE covered
Names the perils that are NOT covered
explanation: A special/open-peril form names what is not covered in its exclusions.

stem: Which peril is one of the ELEVEN basic named perils?
options: Weight of ice, snow or sleet
explanation: External explosion is one of the 11 basic perils; the others listed are broad-form additions.

stem: Inherent vice is best defined as:
options: A property defect that causes it to deteriorate naturally over time
A deductible based on a percentage
explanation: The manual defines inherent vice as the process by which property naturally destroys itself over time, such as rust damage to metal.

stem: A floater is defined as:
options: A limit that applies to one occurrence
A policy for a vacant building
explanation: The manual defines a floater as property of a movable nature.

stem: Loss of rental income after a fire is an example of:
explanation: Lost rent resulting from a direct covered loss is indirect or consequential loss.

stem: Blanket coverage refers to:
options: A policy covering several locations or items under one limit
A separate limit for each scheduled item
Coverage for a vacant building only
explanation: The manual defines blanket coverage as one policy covering several locations or items.

stem: Agreed value endows the insured with:
options: A limit equal to the building's market value
An agreed limit that is the maximum payable even if the loss exceeds it; maintaining it avoids coinsurance on partial losses
Replacement cost on every kind of property
explanation: Agreed value is established by agreement when the policy is issued; the limit is the maximum available even if a loss exceeds it. If maintained, no coinsurance penalty applies to partial losses.

stem: Replacement cost is defined as:
options: The current selling price of a building
The cost to repair or replace using today's labor and material costs
The amount carried divided by amount required
explanation: Replacement cost uses today's labor and material costs. Actual cash value subtracts depreciation.

stem: The vacancy condition in a property policy means:
options: No coverage for every loss immediately when a building is empty
Coverage continues only if a tenant pays rent
No coverage for vandalism or theft after 60 days vacant
explanation: The manual says theft and vandalism are not covered when a property has been vacant over 60 days.

stem: Unoccupied, as used in property policies, means a building:
options: Contains furniture, fixtures, or machinery but no people
Has a tenant who is away for one night
Contains no property and no people
explanation: Unoccupied means no people are present, but furniture, fixtures, or machinery remain.

stem: Under a property policy, the insurer must pay a proven loss within:
options: 30 days after proof of loss, a court judgment, or an appraisal award
explanation: The manual states the insurer must pay within 30 days after proof of loss, judgment, or appraisal award.

stem: In Kansas, an insured generally has how long to sue the insurer after a loss?
explanation: The manual states the insured has up to five years to sue after the loss in Kansas, subject to policy conditions.

stem: If the loss equals or exceeds the policy limits (a total loss), the deductible:
options: Is paid by the mortgage holder
explanation: The manual says the deductible is waived when a loss equals or exceeds the limits (a total loss).

stem: A building worth $200,000 replacement value carries $120,000 and suffers a $40,000 covered loss. The insurer pays:
explanation: The required amount is $160,000 (80% of $200,000). $120,000/$160,000 × $40,000 = $30,000, less any deductible.

stem: Under the co-insurance requirement, the insured must carry:
options: At least 50% of the original purchase price
At least 80% of the building's replacement cost at the time of loss
Any amount shown on the declarations page
explanation: The manual requires coverage of at least 80% of replacement cost at the time of loss.

stem: The appraisal clause provides that:
options: A court must determine every property loss
The insurer always sets the value without review
Each party picks an appraiser and an umpire may be chosen if they disagree
The mortgagee determines the amount of loss
explanation: Each side selects an appraiser; if they cannot agree, they choose a third appraiser called an umpire. The manual says the outcome is binding.

stem: Salvage under a property policy means:
options: The insured transfers recovery rights to the insurer
The company pays replacement cost for all contents
The insured can cancel the policy
The insurer has rights to salvage value after paying for damaged property
explanation: After paying for damaged property, the insurer has rights to salvage value under the manual's description.

stem: 'Our option' gives the insurer the right to:
options: Repair or replace with like kind and quality instead of making a cash settlement
Require an appraisal in every claim
explanation: The insurer need not make a cash settlement; it may repair or replace with like kind and quality.

stem: Subrogation requires the insured to:
options: Transfer their right of recovery against the responsible third party to the insurer
Return undamaged property to the claimant
explanation: Subrogation transfers recovery rights to the insurer, which steps into the insured's shoes.

stem: The Glass replacement provision provides:
options: Actual cash value for all glass
Replacement cost for glass damage, with safety glass where required by ordinance or law
explanation: The manual states replacement cost is provided for glass damage, with safety glass where required by ordinance or law.

stem: GLBA requires a financial institution to:
options: Share all personal information with any third party
Insure customer deposits under property coverage
Cancel policies after a data breach
Give privacy notice and opportunity to opt out before specified disclosure to an unaffiliated third party
explanation: The manual says GLBA limits disclosure of private information to unaffiliated third parties and requires notice and opportunity to opt out.

stem: Loss settlement on a homeowners policy:
options: Pays replacement cost on buildings and ACV on other property, per the manual's example
Pays ACV on buildings and replacement cost on contents
Pays market value for every item
explanation: The manual's HO structure indicates replacement cost on buildings and actual cash value on other property; a contents replacement-cost endorsement is described separately.

stem: The standard property deductible is:
explanation: The manual identifies $250 as the standard dollar deductible and notes total-loss waiver.

stem: Proof of loss must be filed within:
explanation: The manual says to file proof of loss within 60 days, showing value, evidence, and receipts.

stem: A loss settlement of 'actual loss to a pair or set' means:
options: The insurer replaces the entire set regardless of loss
Only one piece of a set can ever be covered
The insurer repairs, replaces, or pays the difference in value before and after the loss if it is not a total loss
explanation: The manual says if it is not a total loss, the insurer repairs, replaces, or pays the difference between value before and after the loss.

stem: Recovered property provisions require the insured to:
options: Return the found property or the amount the company paid
Keep both the found property and the claim payment
explanation: The manual says the insured must either return recovered property or return the amount paid by the company.

stem: Umbrella (excess) liability coverage is described as:
options: Liability coverage providing limits above underlying policies
explanation: An umbrella/excess policy provides liability limits above underlying coverages, subject to its terms.

stem: The personal umbrella policy sits over:
explanation: The personal umbrella sits over underlying personal liability insurance, as illustrated in the manual.

stem: Errors and omissions (E&O) coverage applies to liability arising from:
options: A professional's failure to perform services to appropriate standards
explanation: The manual describes professional liability as protecting against failure to perform hired services or perform them to appropriate standards.

stem: Directors and Officers (D&O) coverage protects:
options: Directors and officers against covered liability arising from their roles
Customers' vehicles at a repair shop
A contractor's promise to complete work
explanation: D&O is a professional liability form for directors and officers' liability exposures.

stem: A fidelity bond protects:
options: A contractor against a customer lawsuit
A business against dishonest acts of employees
explanation: The manual identifies employee dishonesty/fidelity coverage as protection against employees' dishonest acts.

stem: A surety bond is arranged and paid by:
explanation: The principal is the bonded party and typically obtains and pays for the bond; the obligee is protected and the surety backs the promise.

stem: Workers compensation is intended to:
options: Pay only when an employer was negligent
Cover damage to an employer's building
Pay benefits to injured workers regardless of fault or negligence
explanation: The manual states workers compensation pays benefits to injured workers regardless of fault or negligence.

stem: Kansas workers compensation coverage is:
options: A monopolistic system requiring employers to purchase coverage from the state fund
explanation: The manual says employers in a monopolistic state such as Kansas must purchase workers compensation coverage from the state fund.

stem: Medical malpractice coverage may include which clause?
explanation: The manual describes a consent-to-settle clause among the possible medical malpractice policy features.

stem: Employment practices liability (EPL) covers:
options: Employment-related claims such as discrimination or wrongful termination
explanation: EPL protects against suits related to employment practices such as wrongful termination, discrimination, and abuse of employees.

stem: Data breach/cyber liability coverage responds when:
options: An employee is injured at work
A contractor fails to complete a road
A business faces covered liability arising from a data breach
explanation: Cyber/data-breach liability addresses liability arising from data breaches, as noted in the manual.

stem: The Personal Auto Policy's BI coverage pays for:
options: Injuries to others for which an insured is legally responsible
Damage to the insured's own car only
explanation: Bodily injury liability pays for covered injuries to other people for which the insured is legally responsible.

stem: Physical damage coverage on the personal auto policy includes:
explanation: The manual presents physical damage coverages as collision and other-than-collision.

stem: The Business Auto Policy has how many covered auto symbols?
explanation: The manual identifies nine covered-auto symbols.

stem: BAP covered auto symbol 7 provides:
explanation: The manual defines BAP symbol 7 as specifically described autos only, the narrowest coverage symbol.

stem: The garage liability Dealers Form covers:
options: Owned and non-owned autos on a primary basis
Only customer vehicles in a repair shop
explanation: The manual says the Dealers Form covers owned and non-owned autos on a primary basis.

stem: Garagekeepers coverage is:
options: Optional bailee coverage for customer vehicles in the business's custody
explanation: Garagekeepers is optional bailee coverage for customer vehicles left in the business's custody for repair or service.

stem: Which business is eligible for the Business Owners Policy?
explanation: Apartments appear on the manual's eligible list; restaurants, auto repair, and amusement places are ineligible.

stem: Commercial umbrella/excess liability commonly sits over:
options: Commercial liability coverages such as CGL and auto
explanation: The manual's umbrella diagram places excess liability above underlying commercial liability policies.

stem: Boatowners physical damage coverage provides collision and other-than-collision coverage for:
options: The insured boat, motors, trailer, attached equipment, and miscellaneous equipment
A customer's car in a repair shop
explanation: The manual describes boat physical damage for the boat, motors, trailer, attached equipment, and other miscellaneous equipment.

stem: The three parties to a liability policy are:
explanation: The manual identifies the insured, insurer, and party that collects (claimant).

stem: The care, custody and control exclusion excludes damage to:
options: Any property at the insured's address
Property owned, rented, occupied, used, or cared for by the insured
All property owned by a claimant
explanation: The manual describes the exclusion as concerning property owned, rented, occupied, used, or in the insured's care.

stem: Medical payments to others coverage:
options: Pays only after negligence is proven
Pays covered medical expenses to others regardless of fault
explanation: The manual presents medical payments to others as paying regardless of fault to discourage lawsuits.

stem: Punitive damages are:
options: A punishment award, which the manual says is not covered by insurance
explanation: Punitive damages punish and discourage similar wrongdoing; the manual says they are not covered.

stem: Products liability coverage generally requires that the injury:
options: Occur off the business premises (except restaurants), with the product under the customer's control
Be caused by an employee at work
Involve only damage to the defective product itself
explanation: The manual says the injury or damage must occur off premises (except restaurants) and the product must be under the customer's total control.

stem: Completed operations coverage applies:
options: Only to damage to the insured's own tools
After the insured completes the project and leaves, for later injury or damage
Only while the insured is on the premises
explanation: Completed operations applies after the job is complete and the insured has left; the manual calls it an off-premises exposure.

stem: The territory of commercial liability coverage usually includes:
options: Only the premises shown on a homeowners policy
The U.S., possessions, Canada, and international waters and airspace between the territory
explanation: The manual's commercial liability territory includes the U.S., territories/possessions, Puerto Rico, Canada, and international waters and airspace between the territory.

stem: Business income coverage provides:
options: Income for a business interruption caused by a covered peril
A bond to guarantee a contract
explanation: The manual describes business income coverage as income for salaries, payroll, and expenses during a covered interruption.

stem: Extra expense insurance covers:
options: Expenses such as temporary relocation after covered building damage to help prevent income loss
The cost of a surety bond
explanation: The manual describes extra expense as costs incurred when temporarily relocating to prevent income loss after covered damage.

stem: The reporting form's honesty clause:
options: Removes the need for an inventory
Penalizes underreporting by reducing a claim in proportion to the amount underreported
Extends a claim deadline by five years
explanation: The manual says an underreport results in claim payment reduced by the percentage of underreporting.

stem: Burglary coverage under a crime form requires:
options: A missing item with no evidence of crime
Evidence of forced entry into or out of premises or a safe
explanation: Burglary requires evidence of forced entry into or out of premises or a safe.

stem: Robbery, as defined in crime coverage, involves:
options: Taking property by force or threat of bodily harm
A loss without evidence of a crime
explanation: Robbery means taking property by causing or threatening bodily harm.

stem: Employee dishonesty (fidelity) coverage ends for an employee:
options: After a dishonest act by that employee is discovered
explanation: The manual says coverage ends for an employee after a dishonest act has been discovered; discovery period is two years.

stem: Comparative negligence:
options: Bars recovery whenever a plaintiff contributes in any way
Compares the parties' negligence to determine percentage of fault and amount of award
explanation: Comparative negligence compares fault and relates the award to the parties' percentages, per the manual.

stem: The assumption of risk doctrine:
options: Applies only to an insurer's salvage rights
Requires every claim to be paid
Is a form of other insurance
May bar recovery when a plaintiff voluntarily assumes the risk
explanation: The manual says a plaintiff who voluntarily assumes a risk may be barred from recovery.

stem: Intervening cause:
options: May free a defendant from liability when a new proximate cause breaks the chain of events
Is a type of named peril
Means the insurer pays a second deductible
explanation: The manual describes an intervening cause as potentially freeing a defendant of liability when it becomes the proximate cause.

stem: Severability of insurance means:
options: The policy can never be cancelled
Coverage applies separately to each insured, without increasing the limit for one occurrence
Each insured gets a separate policy limit for the same occurrence
explanation: The manual says coverage applies separately to each insured but does not increase the limit for any single occurrence.

stem: A 'split' limit in liability insurance:
options: Combines BI and PD into one limit
Provides separate BI and PD limits that cannot be transferred between them
Is the same as an aggregate
explanation: Split limits separate bodily injury and property damage limits; one cannot be used for the other.

stem: An aggregate limit is:
options: The maximum paid to one injured person
The maximum paid for one event only
A limit for buildings and contents
The maximum paid for all claims combined during a policy period
explanation: Aggregate is the maximum for all claims on behalf of the insured during the policy period.

stem: The definition of 'occupying' for Kansas PIP includes:
options: In, upon, getting in or out, near, under or around the car
Owning the vehicle, regardless of presence
Only driving on a public road
Only sitting in the driver's seat
explanation: The manual's Kansas auto section provides a broad definition of occupying, including in, upon, getting in or out, near, under, or around the car.

stem: According to the manual, Kansas PIP benefits may be paid to:
options: The insured, family members, and occupants of the insured car who do not own a car themselves
Any passenger, including one who owns a car
Only people named on the declarations page
explanation: The manual says PIP benefits are paid to the insured, family, and people occupying the insured car who do not own a car themselves.

stem: Under the Kansas no-fault threshold, a suit for non-pecuniary injuries is allowed only when:
options: The claimant owns the other vehicle
The injury meets a statutory threshold: more than $2,000 in medical bills, a weight-bearing bone injury, permanent disfigurement, or permanent disability
A property claim is also filed
explanation: The manual lists the threshold as more than $2,000 in medical bills, damage to a weight-bearing bone, permanent disfigurement, or permanent disability.

stem: Kansas PIP essential services coverage pays:
options: $25 per day for essential services, with a 365-day minimum coverage period
explanation: The manual lists $25 per day for essential services and states a 365-day minimum coverage period.

stem: Uninsured motorist and underinsured motorist coverage in Kansas requires:
options: Limits lower than bodily injury liability
explanation: The manual says UM/UIM limits must match liability limits.

stem: Kansas requires which auto liability limits?
explanation: The manual states Kansas minimum auto liability limits are 25/50/25.

stem: The Kansas Auto Injury Reparations Act requires that:
options: Every injury be resolved in court
Policies comply with state law and provide required PIP
explanation: The manual says the act requires auto liability policies to comply with state law and requires PIP.

stem: Kansas PIP income and survivors benefits pay:
options: Income: 100% up to $900/month for 12 months; survivors: $900/month for up to 12 months for a spouse and children under 18
explanation: The manual lists disability income at 100% up to $900/month for 12 months and a $900/month survivors benefit for up to 12 months for a spouse and children under 18.

stem: An accident is:
explanation: The manual defines an accident as a sudden and unexpected event.

stem: The Kansas Assigned Risk Insurance Plan (KAIP) requires:
options: Every driver to join a risk pool
Every company doing business must participate and accept its pro-rata share of assignments; an insured must first make three attempts in the normal market
All cars to carry collision coverage
A surety bond for each claim
explanation: The manual says every company doing business must participate in KAIP and accept its pro-rata share of assignments; insureds must make three attempts in the normal market.

stem: Kansas accident prevention course premium reductions last:
options: For the life of the policy
explanation: The manual's Kansas auto section describes the duration of the accident-prevention reduction.

stem: Under the manual, an employer who fails to provide workers compensation coverage when required:
options: Has no liability if the employee was at fault
Must pay the benefits the policy would have paid, may be charged with a misdemeanor and fined, and may owe increased employee benefits as a penalty
explanation: The manual says the employer must pay benefits equal to what the policy would have paid, will be charged with a misdemeanor and fined, and employee benefits will be increased as a further penalty.

stem: The maximum prejudgment interest rate in Kansas is:
explanation: The manual states the maximum prejudgment interest rate in Kansas is 18%.

stem: Kansas commercial policies differ from personal lines in that they:
options: The insurer may cancel for any reason during the first 90 days (60 for personal lines); commercial nonrenewal notice is at least 60 days before the effective date (30 for personal lines)
explanation: The manual gives an initial any-reason cancellation period of 90 days for commercial policies versus 60 days for personal policies, and minimum nonrenewal notice of 60 days for commercial versus 30 days for personal.

stem: The Kansas Homeowners special provisions endorsement:
options: Changes the policy period to five years
Allows five years to sue instead of one year and requires covered losses to be paid within 30 days instead of 60
explanation: The Kansas HO special provisions endorsement gives the insured five years to sue instead of one and requires covered losses to be paid within 30 days instead of 60.

stem: Kansas homeowners ordinance or law coverage is limited to:
options: The market value of the land
explanation: The manual limits ordinance-or-law coverage in Kansas to 10% of the Coverage A limit.

stem: Under Kansas law, an insurer may cancel for any reason during the first:
options: 60 days for personal lines and 90 days for commercial lines
explanation: The manual gives 60 days for personal lines and 90 days for commercial before cancellation is limited to specified reasons.

stem: The manual's basic employers liability limit under Kansas workers compensation is:
explanation: The manual gives a basic employers liability limit of $100,000, which may be increased.

stem: The personal auto policy territory stated in the manual includes:
options: The United States, its territories and possessions, Puerto Rico, and Canada; Mexico is excluded
The United States and Mexico only
explanation: The manual lists the United States, its territories and possessions, Puerto Rico, and Canada, and states there is no coverage in Mexico.

stem: In the HO Section I coverages, Coverage B (Other Structures) is written at:
explanation: The manual's homeowners structure lists Coverage B as an additional 10% of Coverage A.

stem: HO Coverage D, Loss of Use, is described in the manual as:
options: Consequential or indirect-loss coverage, such as additional living expenses or loss of rent
explanation: Coverage D addresses consequential loss, including additional living expenses or loss of rent.

stem: Unscheduled personal property under HO Coverage C is settled on which basis?
options: Actual cash value (replacement cost less depreciation)
explanation: The manual's HO structure identifies Coverage C as ACV; a replacement-cost endorsement is described separately.

stem: The Scheduled Personal Property endorsement on an HO policy provides:
options: Only liability for a scheduled item
Specified limits, agreed value with no deductible, and worldwide open-peril coverage for scheduled property
explanation: The manual says this endorsement provides specified limits for scheduled property, agreed value without a deductible, and open-peril coverage worldwide.

stem: The water back-up and sump pump discharge/overflow endorsement on an HO policy provides:
options: Coverage for every flood loss automatically
Up to $5,000 of coverage with a $250 deductible
explanation: The manual states that the water-backup and sump pump endorsement provides up to $5,000 of coverage with a $250 deductible.

stem: The Personal Injury endorsement sold with the homeowners policy covers:
options: Listed personal-injury offenses such as defamation
explanation: The manual's homeowners section describes a personal-injury endorsement for listed offenses, distinct from bodily injury/property damage liability.

stem: Personal inland marine (a personal article floater) is written for:
options: Movable valuables such as jewelry, furs, or guns
explanation: The manual gives personal article floaters for movable valuables such as guns, jewelry, and furs.

stem: Which Commercial Inland Marine coverage class covers property in the care, custody and control of the business, such as a dry cleaner's customer's clothes?
explanation: Bailee's customer coverage addresses customers' property in a business's care, custody, and control.

stem: Which statement about the Contractors Equipment Floater is correct?
options: It covers only a contractor's building
It is a homeowners liability endorsement
It insures only money in transit
It is a listed commercial inland marine class for contractors' equipment
explanation: The manual lists contractors equipment floater among commercial inland marine classes.

stem: Inland marine for instruments of communication and transportation is used for:
options: Bridges, tunnels, docks, pipelines, towers, and transmission lines
explanation: The manual lists structures and systems such as bridges, tunnels, docks, pipelines, towers, and power transmission lines.

stem: Under a Domestic Shipments & Transportation Floater, business personal property is NOT covered when it is:
options: More than 100 feet from the premises
explanation: The manual notes the 100-foot limit for business personal property under this coverage.

stem: The Commercial/Business Owners Policy coverage territory for business personal property is:
options: The U.S., possessions, Puerto Rico, and Canada, provided the property is within 100 feet of the premises
explanation: The manual gives this territory and the within-100-feet condition for business personal property.

stem: The single most important difference between a special (open peril) form and a named peril form is that the special form:
options: Names the causes that are excluded
explanation: A special/open form names exclusions; a named-peril form names the perils covered.

stem: Earthquake coverage can be added by endorsement. The manual states the deductible typically ranges:
explanation: The manual states earthquake deductible commonly ranges from 2-10% of the amount of coverage, applying separately to covered structures.

stem: Flood coverage is available through:
explanation: The manual says flood coverage can be purchased through the federal National Flood Insurance Program.

stem: The vacancy condition in a property policy denies coverage for vandalism or theft when the property has been:
options: Insured for more than one year
explanation: The manual says vandalism or theft are not covered when vacant beyond 60 days.

stem: Under the manual's definitions, a property is VACANT when it is:
options: Empty of both people and contents
explanation: Vacant means empty of both people and contents; unoccupied means people are absent but contents remain.

stem: The restoration of limits condition means:
options: After a loss, limits are restored for future losses
The deductible is refunded after every loss
The policy automatically doubles its limit
explanation: The manual states that limits are restored after a loss for future losses.

stem: In the other-insurance condition for property, the scheduled coverage is:
options: Always primary, with unscheduled coverage excess
explanation: The manual states scheduled coverage is primary and unscheduled coverage is excess.

stem: Which of these is a duty the insured owes after a property loss?
options: Repair everything before contacting the insurer
Notify the insurer, protect property from further damage, and file proof of loss
Transfer the policy without written consent
explanation: The manual lists notice, protecting property from further loss, and filing proof of loss with supporting information.

stem: The three coverages written by the Commercial Crime ('02) form are:
options: Workers compensation, employers liability, and umbrella
Employee dishonesty, inside-the-premises money/securities, and forgery/alteration
explanation: The manual's crime section lists employee dishonesty, inside-the-premises theft/robbery-related coverages, and forgery/alteration among the coverage forms.

stem: In crime insurance, BURGLARY is best described as:
options: Taking property with evidence of forced entry into or out of a premises or safe
Taking property through threat of bodily harm
explanation: Burglary requires evidence of forced entry into or out of a premises or safe.

stem: EXTORTION, as defined for commercial crime coverage, is:
options: Surrender of property away from premises due to a threat to harm a person being held captive
The disappearance of an inventory item
explanation: The manual defines extortion as surrendering property away from the premises as a result of a threat to harm you, an employee, or a captive relative.

stem: In crime terminology, the difference between a CUSTODIAN and a MESSENGER is:
options: Custodian is always a claimant; messenger is an insurer
Custodian handles claims; messenger sells policies
Custodian has care of property inside the premises; messenger has care outside
explanation: The manual distinguishes a custodian inside the premises from a messenger outside.

stem: MYSTERIOUS DISAPPEARANCE in crime coverage means:
options: A policy limit has been exhausted
Property is missing but there is no evidence a crime occurred
explanation: Mysterious disappearance means property is missing without evidence that a crime occurred.

stem: Employee dishonesty under the fidelity bond stops for a given employee:
options: After a dishonest act has been discovered
explanation: Coverage ends for an employee after that employee's dishonest act is discovered; the manual describes a two-year discovery period.

stem: In a surety bond arrangement, who pays for the bond?
explanation: The principal is the party whose obligation is bonded and typically pays for the surety bond.

stem: Which profession is NOT among the classes for which the manual lists E&O coverage as available?
explanation: The manual lists advertisers/broadcasters/publishers, insurance agents, accountants, real estate agents and brokers, architects/engineers, attorneys, pension plan fiduciaries, and stockbrokers; it does not list plumbers.

stem: Under the lawyers form of E&O, member attorneys of the firm:
options: Become obligees on a surety bond
Are covered only for auto claims
Are automatically covered as named insureds without being individually named
explanation: The manual says the lawyers E&O form automatically covers all member attorneys of the firm as named insureds without naming them individually.

stem: The medical malpractice coverage form may include which clause?
explanation: The manual lists a consent-to-settle clause as a feature that may appear in medical malpractice coverage.

stem: The two forms of commercial general liability differ in when the claim must be made. Under the CLAIMS MADE form:
options: Only the occurrence must be during the policy period
Both the occurrence and claim must meet the policy's timing requirements
The claim can be made at any time, regardless of occurrence date
explanation: The manual says both occurrence and claim must be during the policy period for claims-made coverage, subject to endorsements such as retroactive date and ERP.

stem: The BASIC Extended Reporting Period on a claims-made CGL policy:
options: Is an unlimited extension that must be purchased
Is automatically included and allows 60 days to report an occurrence; claims arising from occurrences reported in that window may be made during the following five years
Applies only to new occurrences after policy expiration
explanation: The manual describes the basic ERP as automatically included, with 60-day reporting and a five-year period for claims from occurrences reported in that period.

stem: The SUPPLEMENTAL Extended Reporting Period:
options: Is another name for a retroactive date
Is purchased as an option and provides an unlimited extension for claims from covered-period occurrences
explanation: The supplemental ERP is optional, begins after the basic ERP, and provides an unlimited reporting extension for claims from occurrences during the policy period.

stem: The RETROACTIVE DATE endorsement on a claims-made form:
options: Sets how far into the past prior occurrences may be covered
Changes an occurrence form into a property form
explanation: The retroactive date limits how far into the past coverage is afforded for prior occurrences.

stem: ADVERTISING INJURY, as defined in the commercial liability basic hazards, covers:
options: Bodily injury caused by any advertisement
Specified offenses such as certain defamation or infringement in advertising
Physical damage to the insured's own product
explanation: The manual describes advertising injury as specified offenses, including listed defamation, privacy, advertising idea, and slogan matters.

stem: PERSONAL INJURY, as defined in the commercial liability basic hazards, covers:
options: Listed offenses such as wrongful entry or eviction and false arrest, distinct from BI/PD
explanation: The manual lists wrongful entry/eviction and false arrest among personal injury offenses and distinguishes them from BI/PD.

stem: FIRE LEGAL (tenant liability) coverage covers:
options: Every fire loss to the whole building regardless of cause
Damage to the tenant's own contents only
Covered damage for which an insured may be liable to the rented part of a building
explanation: The manual describes fire legal as covering specified damage to the part of a building leased or rented for which the insured may be liable.

stem: MEDICAL PAYMENTS TO OTHERS on the commercial liability form pays:
options: Medical bills of others regardless of negligence, subject to the stated terms and limits
Only an insured's own medical bills
Only after a lawsuit proves negligence
explanation: The manual says medical payments to others pay others' medical bills regardless of negligence to discourage lawsuits.

stem: For products liability to attach under a CGL policy:
options: The claimant must be an employee
The product must be under the customer's total control and the injury must occur off premises, except for restaurants
Only the product itself must be damaged
The insured must still be making the product
explanation: The manual gives off-premises injury (with restaurant exception) and customer control as requirements in its products liability discussion.

stem: Under completed operations coverage:
options: Only property owned by the contractor is insured
Coverage applies only while the insured is doing the work
The insured must have completed the project and left before the occurrence
The claim must be made before the job starts
explanation: Completed operations applies after the project is finished and the insured has left; injury before completion is operations exposure.

stem: In Kansas, the limits for UNINSURED MOTORIST and UNDERINSURED MOTORIST coverage must be:
explanation: The manual says UM/UIM limits must match liability limits.

stem: Under the Kansas no-fault threshold, what amount of medical bills meets the medical-expense condition for suing for non-pecuniary injuries?
explanation: The manual's medical-expense threshold is more than $2,000; exactly $2,000 does not meet that condition.

stem: Kansas requires the driver to carry proof of insurance consisting of:
options: An insurance card with the insurer's name, policy number, effective and expiration dates, or a certificate of self-insurance signed by the Insurance Commissioner
A surety bond for every trip
explanation: The manual requires a card stating the insurer's name, policy number, effective date, and expiration date, or a certificate of self-insurance signed by the Insurance Commissioner.

stem: Kansas is described in the manual as a monopolistic workers compensation state. That means employers:
options: Can replace workers compensation with homeowners insurance
Must purchase workers compensation coverage from the Kansas state fund
explanation: The manual identifies Kansas as a monopolistic workers compensation state, where employers must purchase coverage from the state fund.

stem: Motorcycle operators in Kansas:
options: May reject required PIP coverage, which reduces the premium
Are covered by homeowners Coverage C
Are automatically exempt from all Kansas auto insurance requirements
explanation: The manual says Kansas motorcycle operators may reject PIP, reducing the premium; this does not exempt them from every auto insurance rule.

stem: Kansas rules on the territory of the personal auto policy provide coverage:
options: The United States, its territories and possessions, Puerto Rico, and Canada; there is no coverage in Mexico
explanation: The manual lists the United States, its territories and possessions, Puerto Rico, and Canada, and explicitly excludes Mexico.

stem: Under the Kansas property policy provision, the insured may sue the insurer:
options: After complying with all policy provisions and within five years after the loss
Immediately after a claim is reported
explanation: The manual allows up to five years to sue after the loss in Kansas, but says the insured cannot sue until all policy provisions have been complied with.

stem: The Kansas HO special provisions endorsement requires that covered losses be paid:
options: Within 30 days, instead of the usual 60 days
explanation: The Kansas HO special provisions endorsement requires covered losses to be paid within 30 days rather than the usual 60 days.

stem: Under KSA 40-3-22, inland marine may NOT insure:
options: Merchandise held in storage or during manufacture, building improvements, and specified money/securities
explanation: The manual lists those excluded categories under KSA 40-3-22.

stem: Kansas limits ordinance or law coverage to:
explanation: The manual limits Kansas ordinance-or-law coverage to 10% of the Coverage A limit.

stem: The maximum prejudgment interest rate permitted in Kansas is:
explanation: The manual states the maximum prejudgment interest rate in Kansas is 18%.

stem: Property that may be written on an inland marine form in Kansas includes:
explanation: Contractors equipment appears as a commercial inland marine class; the manual separately lists property barred by state law.

stem: Kansas nonpayment of premium cancellation requires at least:
explanation: The manual gives a minimum 10-day notice for nonpayment of premium.

stem: Kansas commercial policies require at least how much notice of nonrenewal?
explanation: The manual requires a minimum of 60 days' notice for commercial nonrenewal (30 days for personal policies).

stem: An insurer may cancel a Kansas personal lines policy for ANY reason during the first:
explanation: The manual says personal policies may be cancelled for any reason during the first 60 days; commercial is 90 days.

stem: Four of the ten blueprint subjects on this exam are Kansas statutes and regulations. Altogether how many of the 140 exam questions do they account for?
explanation: The manual's test breakdown gives four Kansas statute blocks: 19 + 7 + 7 + 7 = 40 questions.

stem: The test breakdown lists the subject matter of the four Kansas statute and regulation blocks in:
options: The Pre-Study Guide plus the specific manual sections cited for some subjects
explanation: The manual test breakdown points to the Pre-Study Guide and relevant chapters/sections; the attached Book #2 does not contain every referenced item.

stem: The blueprint subject that carries the MOST questions is:
options: Types of property policies and types of casualty policies/bonds (25 each)
explanation: The test breakdown assigns 25 questions each to types of property policies and types of casualty policies/bonds.

stem: You have 150 minutes for 140 questions. About how much time should you budget per question?
explanation: 150 minutes × 60 seconds ÷ 140 questions is about 64 seconds per question.

stem: According to the test breakdown, the seven questions on Kansas statutes pertinent to casualty insurance reference:
explanation: The test breakdown lists sections 3.1-3.2 and 4.1-4.7 as the references for the seven Kansas statutes questions pertinent to casualty insurance.

stem: Three families of law can bar recovery on a claim. A plaintiff who knowingly rides in the back of a pickup is invoking:
explanation: The manual uses an adult voluntarily riding in the back of a pickup as its example of assumption of risk.

stem: The SPECIAL PROVISIONS KANSAS ENDORSEMENT required on the HO policy is:
options: The same special provisions Kansas endorsement required on the dwelling policy (DP)
explanation: The manual says the special provisions Kansas endorsement required on the dwelling policy is the same endorsement required on the homeowners policy.

stem: Under the common policy conditions, the first named insured may cancel the policy:
options: By written notice at any time
explanation: The manual says the insured or first named insured may cancel at any time in writing.

stem: After a kitchen fire, Lena asks her agent why the policy contract names both her and an insurance company. Which explanation best describes property insurance in this example?
options: It is a contract between the insured and insurer for covered property loss, subject to its terms and limits
It is a three-party contract between a claimant, court, and fire department
It guarantees every kind of loss, regardless of peril
It pays only for injuries to people
explanation: Property insurance is a two-party contract between insured and insurer. A covered loss is loss caused by a covered peril, and payment is limited by the policy.

stem: A covered fire damages Omar's apartment building, and the tenants' rent stops while repairs are made. Which description best distinguishes the two financial effects?
options: Both are liability claims because tenants lost money
Building damage is direct loss; the resulting rental-income loss is indirect or consequential loss
Lost rent is direct physical damage; the fire is an indirect loss
explanation: Physical damage from the fire is direct loss. The lost rent that follows because the building cannot be used is indirect (consequential) loss.

stem: A policy says it covers only causes specifically listed. A wind peril is not on the list, and wind damages a shed. What is the first coverage question?
options: Whether the building is vacant for 60 days
Whether the insured has liability coverage
Whether wind appears among the named perils on that form
Whether the insured chose replacement cost
explanation: A named-peril form covers listed causes only. Since the question says wind is absent, check the named-peril grant before considering other claim details.

stem: A special/open-peril form covers direct physical loss unless an exclusion applies. An unusual object falls onto a covered roof, and no exclusion is stated in the facts. What is the best next step?
options: Assume all special-form claims are excluded
Pay only if the peril is fire
Treat the loss as liability to the object owner
Check the exclusions rather than searching for the falling object on a named-peril list
explanation: An open-peril form starts with direct physical loss and names exclusions. The form is not unlimited, so exclusions must still be checked.

stem: A customer slips on a wet floor at Nora's shop and later sends a demand for medical bills. Which three parties describe the liability claim?
options: Nora, her insurer, and the customer/claimant
Nora, the property owner, and the fire department
The customer, the judge, and the policy broker
Nora, a surety, and an obligee
explanation: A liability policy has the insured, insurer, and party that collects-the claimant. The claimant here is the injured customer.

stem: A repair shop damages a customer's watch while the watch is in the shop's care for repair. Which liability-policy issue should the adjuster check?
options: The care, custody, and control exclusion for property in the insured's care
explanation: The manual describes an exclusion for damage to property owned, rented, used, or in the insured's care, custody, and control. The watch was in the shop's care.

stem: A lightning strike damages the detached garage behind a home. Which HO Section I coverage letter is the natural starting point?
explanation: Coverage B is for other structures, including a detached garage. The cause of loss and policy wording must still be checked separately.

stem: An HO-3 insured reports an unexplained accidental break to a wall attached to the home and to a camera in the living room. Which comparison is accurate before checking exclusions?
options: Both are automatically open-peril because all HO-3 letters match
Both are Section II liability claims
The wall is Coverage B and the camera is Coverage D
The wall is Coverage A on special form; the camera is Coverage C on broad named perils
explanation: HO-3 uses special/open peril for Coverage A and broad named perils for Coverage C. The cause-of-loss rules differ by coverage letter.

stem: A tenant insures furniture and clothing but does not own the apartment building. Which form in the manual's comparison fits this household?
explanation: HO-4 is the renters form; it does not require dwelling or other-structures coverage and insures the tenant's personal property.

stem: A landlord insures a rental dwelling with a DP-2. The tenant's belongings are stolen. Which statement is supported by the manual?
options: The DP automatically insures the tenant's personal property
The dwelling policy is property coverage and specifically excludes theft of personal property
The DP is a package policy with renters liability
The loss is automatically paid under Coverage F
explanation: The manual says dwelling policies specifically exclude theft coverage for personal property. A tenant's property should not be assumed covered by the landlord's DP.

stem: A $300,000 building has an 80% coinsurance requirement. The insured carries $180,000 and has a covered $40,000 loss. Before any deductible, how much does the formula pay?
explanation: The required amount is $240,000. $180,000 divided by $240,000 is 0.75; 0.75 × $40,000 = $30,000 before deductible.

stem: A building contains furniture and machinery, but its occupants are away on a long trip. Which manual definition best fits?
options: Vacant, because no people are present
Neither term applies to a building
Vacant and unoccupied mean the same thing
Unoccupied, because contents remain but people are absent
explanation: The manual defines unoccupied as a building containing furniture, fixtures, or machinery but not people. Vacant means no contents and no people.

stem: A warehouse employee strains her back while lifting a box during her scheduled shift. Under the purpose statement in the manual, what is central to workers compensation?
options: Benefits for covered injured workers regardless of fault or negligence
Whether the worker owns the warehouse
Whether the employee can prove the employer intended the injury
Whether the employer has a surety bond
explanation: The manual states the purpose of workers compensation is to pay benefits to injured workers regardless of fault or negligence.

stem: After a covered work injury, an employee also brings a common-law claim against the employer. Which policy part in the manual addresses that kind of employer claim?
explanation: The manual describes Part One as Workers Compensation and Part Two as Employers Liability for common-law claims against the employer.

stem: A city requires a contractor to guarantee performance. The contractor is bonded, the city is protected, and a bond company backs the promise. Name the city and contractor's roles, respectively.
explanation: The protected party is the obligee; the contractor whose obligation is bonded is the principal. The surety backs the promise.

stem: A small firm's general liability limit is exhausted by a covered claim. It bought an umbrella policy to provide additional liability limits above underlying coverage. What role is the umbrella intended to serve?
options: Pay employee medical expenses regardless of fault
Provide excess liability limits over underlying policies, subject to its terms
explanation: The manual describes umbrella/excess coverage as additional liability protection above underlying policies. Its terms and attachment requirements still apply.

stem: A visitor voluntarily rides in the back of a pickup after being warned it is unsafe. The visitor is hurt. Which defense does the manual's example most closely illustrate?
explanation: The manual uses an adult riding in the back of a pickup as its example of voluntarily assuming a risk.

stem: One accident injures three people. The policy has a per-occurrence limit and a lower per-person limit. Which statement should guide the claim analysis?
options: The per-occurrence limit applies separately to each person
Check the per-person cap for each claimant and the per-occurrence cap for the event
The aggregate limit is the only limit that matters
A split limit allows bodily-injury limits to pay property damage
explanation: Per-person limits cap payment for one individual; per-occurrence limits cap the event. Both may apply to the same multi-claimant loss.

stem: A passenger is hurt in a Kansas crash. Before the drivers resolve who was at fault, which coverage is designed to provide specified first-party benefits under the manual?
explanation: Kansas PIP is a no-fault benefit coverage described by the manual; collision addresses physical damage to an insured auto.

stem: A driver accidentally hits a parked car and is legally responsible for the other owner's injuries. Which PAP coverage category is the first liability match?
options: Medical payments to others under a CGL
explanation: Bodily injury liability addresses injuries to other people for which the insured is legally responsible. Collision is first-party physical damage to the insured auto.

stem: A Kansas driver has liability limits of 25/50/25. What must the UM/UIM limits match, according to the manual?
explanation: The manual states Kansas UM/UIM limits must match the liability limits.

stem: A Kansas claimant has $2,300 in medical bills after a collision and seeks non-pecuniary damages. Under the manual's threshold, which conclusion is correct?
options: The suit is barred because only property damage counts
The medical-bill threshold is met because the bills exceed $2,000
The threshold is met only if bills exceed $4,500
A collision deductible determines whether the suit is allowed
explanation: The manual's medical-bill threshold is more than $2,000; $2,300 exceeds it. The manual also lists weight-bearing bone injury, permanent disfigurement, and permanent disability as threshold conditions.

stem: A customer leaves a car at a repair shop for service. The car is damaged while in the shop's custody. Which coverage is designed for that customer-vehicle exposure?
explanation: Garagekeepers is optional bailee coverage for damage to customer vehicles left in the business's custody for repair or service.

stem: A delivery company asks whether a particular van is covered under its BAP. What policy detail should be matched to the van and coverage at issue?
options: The covered-auto symbol shown for that coverage
explanation: The BAP uses covered-auto symbols to identify which autos are covered for each coverage. Match the applicable symbol rather than assuming all autos are covered.

stem: A neighborhood apartment building is six stories and within the BOP ceilings stated in the manual. Which additional question still matters before concluding it qualifies?
options: Whether the business is on the manual's eligible-occupancy list
Whether it has a homeowners Coverage C
Whether a claimant signed a bond
Whether the building is in a flood zone only
explanation: BOP eligibility requires both qualifying occupancy and compliance with size ceilings. Being under the limits alone is not enough.

stem: A contractor's portable machine travels from job site to job site. Which manual concept is the strongest starting point for protecting this movable business property?
options: Commercial inland marine contractors equipment floater
explanation: The manual lists contractors equipment floater as a commercial inland marine class, fitting movable equipment exposure.

stem: A contractor's crew is still installing cabinets when a falling tool injures the homeowner. The project is not finished and the crew has not left. Which exposure does the manual point to?
explanation: Completed operations begins after the project is finished and the insured has left. An injury before completion is treated as operations exposure in the manual.

stem: A claims-made policy expires today. A covered-period occurrence is reported during the basic ERP's 60-day window. Which consequence matches the manual's description?
options: The supplemental ERP is automatically unlimited
The policy covers every new accident for five years
The retroactive date automatically moves forward
A five-year period applies to claims resulting from that reported occurrence
explanation: The manual describes a 60-day reporting window and a five-year period for claims arising from occurrences reported during that window.

stem: A warehouse manager finds a stock shortage after taking inventory. There are no broken locks, witnesses, or other signs of a crime. Which crime term best fits the facts as given?
explanation: Mysterious disappearance means property is missing but there is no evidence a crime occurred. Burglary requires evidence of forced entry; robbery involves force or threat.

stem: An employee carries company cash from the office to the bank. Which crime-policy role describes the employee while in custody of property outside the premises?
explanation: The manual defines a messenger as an employee or other listed person with care and custody of property outside the premises; a custodian is inside.
